paragraphs: The core work of retail loss prevention specialists is to trace leads on merchandise or cash loss, patrol store and warehouse risks, check inventory discrepancies and monitoring systems, and record facts, sources, times, and handling receipts in incident reports. values: Materials and setup｜a completely fictional store loss prevention tabletop exercise

You are a loss prevention trainee at a fictional store and may only check the A1—A5 records, list suspicious points, and report to the duty supervisor. The material contains no real customer or employee information; no detention, search, disciplinary, or police reporting decision is made by the trainee.

A1｜Tuesday handover sheet: SKU-R8 wireless earphones show system inventory of 20 and a physical count of 18; the count time is 18:00 and the recorder code is C1. The discrepancy has not yet been reviewed.

A2｜transaction summary: 1 sold that day, 1 customer return pending quality inspection; a transfer record for 1 unit shows shipped but there is no receiving receipt. Each system was updated at different times.

A3｜the surveillance index notes only that the receiving area footage is missing for 5 minutes at 17:20; there is no conclusion about anyone's identity or behavior. The equipment log indicates the camera was briefly offline, and the cause has not been confirmed.

A4｜a colleague says verbally that maybe someone took the earphones, with no incident time or original voucher; a customer is in a dispute at the exit, and the on-site safety status has not been checked.

A5｜fictional store protocol: the trainee attends to personal safety first and must not pursue, search, or accuse; original records are shown only to the authorized supervisor. The supervisor is responsible for on-site judgment, contacting security or police when necessary, and keeping a takeover receipt.
Task and outputs

Using A1—A5, build a one-page discrepancy checklist: list the physical count, sales, returns, transfers, system update times, footage gap, verbal statements, and still-unknown items separately; the 2-unit discrepancy must not be written directly as theft.

Then write a safety escalation card: mark the customer dispute, the surveillance interruption, the time the supervisor was notified, the person taking over, and the next review; do not invent identities, footage content, or your own handling steps.
Reference approach (complete it independently first)

A1's 20 versus 18 is only a count discrepancy. A2 requires checking at least sales, return quality inspection, transfer receiving receipts, and timestamps; the cause of loss cannot be determined before these records reconcile.

A3 has only a footage gap and an offline equipment log and cannot be used to infer who did what; per permissions, ask the supervisor to arrange an equipment check and preserve the available original records.

The verbal statement in A4 is an unverified lead, and for the customer dispute the supervisor is notified first per the A5 safety protocol. Handover should state what is known, unknown, the time, material location, notification recipients, and takeover confirmation; the trainee does not pursue or accuse.

All material is fictional; surveillance, background checks, searches, or detention must not be carried out on that basis. Real incidents must be handled per local law, employer policy, and on-site safety protocols; a tabletop work product only explains checking and handover thinking.

subject.summary: Retail loss prevention specialists check inventory discrepancies in stores or distribution, patrol for merchandise and entrance and exit risks, inspect loss prevention processes and monitoring equipment, and record, investigate, and escalate anomalies as authorized. Incident handling must balance customer and employee safety with the integrity of evidence; on-site detention authority must be verified against local law and employer policy.
